wave: W2 — the TeamExecutor seam (native default, official fallback)

toolchain.note: the manifest's pinned buildToolchain, first on PATH

delivered: DshTeamExecutor in mpd-dsh-adapter: kind, reason, providers(), spawn(), send(), interrupt(), membership(), members() — every method total, a refusal carrying a sentence

the NATIVE backend (DEFAULT): ctx.subagents.startContinuable + sendMessage + interrupt, with the PROVIDER and the member's agentOptions chosen BY THE CALLER — the two arguments the official tool row cannot forward, and therefore the whole point
the OFFICIAL backend (FALLBACK): the dsh.team* calls, kept as a real implementation because it owns the roster (a member raised by another row is still identified) and adjacency-checks delivery
capabilities().teamExecutorNative — the pre-flight flag, read with the SAME predicate teamExecutor() uses so the two cannot disagree
MPD_DSH_TEAM_EXECUTOR=native|official — a DIAGNOSIS override that FALLS THROUGH when the named backend cannot serve, so it can never hand back a broken backend

the mpd team record is now the BOARD for BOTH backends: approve raises members through the executor and posts NO task anywhere; dispatch and claim read the record; mail resolves the handle the executor recorded
why_it_matters: In a dsh-tui composition the official service cannot mount at all, so before this wave the bundle's team plane could not raise a member there. The native default needs nothing from the official plugin.
measured_findings: subagents is a HOST-plane service and mpd-team-core can apply BEFORE it is ACTIVE, so an apply-time read answers 'unavailable' in a healthy composition (evidence/dsh-qa/preset-conformance/*/boot.log). The TOOLS were never affected — every call re-resolves the executor lazily, which is why that is the design — but the LOG LINE was, and it now re-reports on the binding.

the D6 gate reported the first version of that deferred binding: naming the official service by string outside the adapter is exactly what it forbids. Only `subagents` is named now, and nothing is lost — the executor re-resolves its backend on every call.
editing the adapter's SOURCE changes the built bytes of 19 other packages, because bun build inlines the relative imports. Every one had to be rebuilt; verify-dist-fresh names them.

tests.summary: 1301 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail — 120 files, 12391 expect() calls (16 executor arms + 12 core arms among them)

d6-no-direct-team-access.summary: PASS — 0 findings; it CAUGHT one during this wave and the code was changed, not the gate

typecheck.summary: 4 errors, ALL pre-existing in skills/programming/scripts/typescript/check-no-excuse-rules.ts — none new

mount_boot.proves: in a REAL isolated boot the active backend resolves to NATIVE: the boot log carries 'team executor: native (native: the default backend — it needs nothing from the official plugin)'. The apply-time line reads UNAVAILABLE first, which is the measured host-plane ordering above and is why the report is deferred.

not_claimed: no LIVE teammate was raised: the executor is proven by arms against harness doubles and by the resolution in a real boot, not by a model call (this environment holds no credentials, per §7 the sandbox must not hold any).
the official backend's arms drive a double, so its behaviour against the real service is unchanged from W1 rather than re-proven.
